# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–7 (Complete and Final – Updated 79)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, Wilhaven, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, hill farms of Coldcombe, Humdrum Hall, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Prince Regent locations, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, hill farms of Fenmere, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, Hants, Life Guards
- **Narrative Presence**: Narrator warns Vanity Fair is "a very vain, wicked, foolish place, full of all sorts of humbugs and falsenesses and pretensions"; observes human hearts and self-deceptions with ironic sympathy

## Main Characters

**Dorothea and Will Ladislaw (Married)**
- Married with infant son; established pattern of two yearly visits to Grange

**Mary Garth and Fred Garth (Married)**
- Inhabit Stone Court in white-haired placidity; Fred distinguished county farmer

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy; mother French opera-girl
- Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; white slender fingers
- Skilled musician, linguist, artist; speaks French with purity; proficient in globes
- Determined, observant, capable of calculated charm; "I might go farther, and fare worse"
- **Governess at Queen's Crawley**: Governess to Rose and Violet; treats Lady Crawley with cool respect; plays backgammon with Sir Pitt; shows respectful obedience to Mr. Pitt Crawley; writes Sir Pitt's letters, manages accounts; has upper hand of entire house
- **Relationship with Miss Crawley**: Won her heart upon arrival; made conquest during Mudbury drive; Miss Crawley now demands Rebecca sit at dinners despite governess status; calls her "little paragon—positively a little jewel"; says Rebecca has more brains than half the shire; treats as equal while making her run errands, read her to sleep nightly with French novels
- **Relationship with Rawdon Crawley**: Captain Rawdon has distinguished her many times; hung over her piano; written her notes; Rebecca popped first note into fire; Rawdon has declined entertainments, would not dine with mess; great pleasure strolling to Rectory with Miss Crawley; evening walks charming in moonlight; at river crossing in Gulton, Rebecca tasted cigar "in prettiest way possible"; Old Sir Pitt espied pair and swore great oaths; Rawdon increasingly attached; Miss Crawley orders Rawdon lead her in to dinner, Rebecca follow with cushion
- **Joseph Sedley Romance**: Upon learning of wealth, determined to marry him; won household; Jos began eloquent speech but stopped when music ended; at Vauxhall took Jos's arm; during inebriation Jos shouted "Stop, my dearest diddle-diddle-darling"; George Osborne pushed Jos back; Jos never came; household (except Amelia) turned against her; Blenkinsop reported her reading Mrs. Sedley's letters and accessing trinket boxes
- **Recent Developments**: Now in London at Miss Crawley's residence in Park Lane; attending Miss Crawley during illness; dismissed Miss Briggs from sickroom; took over nursing duties; ate dinner with Miss Briggs and managed her emotions with calculated sympathy; assured Briggs she would return to Queen's Crawley after Miss Crawley recovered; Briggs felt displacement despite Rebecca's reassurance; Rebecca went upstairs to patient's rooms; eliminated Mrs. Firkin from nursing role
- **Current Status**: Successfully positioned as Miss Crawley's companion/nurse in London; gaining influence over household staff; maintaining courteous but controlling presence

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome brother of Amelia Sedley; believed by society to be infatuated with her
- Jolly, sociable; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports, song, parade; adored by men; famous drinker and sparrer; won Garrison cup
- **Actual Behavior vs. Public Perception**: Despite society supposing him at Amelia's feet, frequently NOT with her; plays billiards with Captain Cannon in Swallow Street while Amelia awaits him; lit cigar with Amelia's letter to Dobbin's horror; convinced Misses Osborne he makes romantic sacrifice; pushed Jos back at Vauxhall
- **Secret Liaisons**: For some time strove to keep secret; admitted "there was a woman in the case"; judge's daughter at Demerara; beautiful quadroon girl Miss Pye at St. Vincent's; reputation as "regular Don Giovanni" prodigious amongst young officers
- **Engagement to Amelia**: Has admitted engagement to Captain Dobbin and Mrs. Major O'Dowd; became furious upon learning regiment knows; confronted Dobbin believing him betrayer; upon reflection, apologized; admits "I am very fond of Amelia; I adore her"; acknowledges "She's faultless"; insists "there's no fun in winning a thing unless you play for it"; claims "the regiment's just back from the West Indies, I must have a little fling, and then when I'm married I'll reform"
- **Recent Developments**: Took tender leave of Amelia morning after visiting Osborne house; hurried to City; visited Mr. Chopper, his father's head man; received document; exchanged document at Hulker & Bullock's for pocketful of money; was "much too elated" to notice old John Sedley leaving banker's parlour looking dismal; George much too pleased with financial transaction to mark Sedley's depression
- **Financial Status**: Over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate; shot Captain Marker in duel; robbed young Lord Dovedale at Cocoa-Tree; Dobbin has assisted him financially; receives allowance; relies on Dobbin's loans; out of cash until father provides funds; **recently received money from father via Mr. Chopper (CHANGED)**
- **Father's Position**: Old Mr. Osborne wealthy merchant in tallow trade and City of London; believes good society cannot go wrong; has ordered George to avoid gambling or be cut off with shilling; recently warned George: unless Amelia's ten thousand pounds is settled down, George cannot marry her; states "I'll have no lame duck's daughter in my family"; claims Sedley's affairs look bad; instructed George to call on Mr. Chopper in City for money

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Rebecca's former schoolfriend at Chiswick; spurned by discriminating sex despite school friendships
- Small, modest, unaffected young creature; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul like violet
- **Relationship with George**: Became object of his attentions; confirmed engagement when speaking to young Bullock; believes deeply in George; innocent and trusting; when George runs errands, Amelia waits believing him at Horse Guards, Chatham, or obliged to see friends; assumes he too tired to write long letters; loves George completely and trustingly; does not doubt him
- **Actual Behavior**: Leaves home daily; dines abroad six days week; neglected twelve dear Chiswick friends; single subject to think about; made confidante of little Laura Martin; promised Laura would live with her when married
- **Letters to George**: Extraordinarily long and passionate; filled sheets of large paper crossed with astonishing perverseness; wrote whole pages of poetry without pity; underlined words with frantic emphasis; repetitive; doubtful grammar; took liberties with metre; numerous notes followed him; ordered servant deliver only to private apartment
- **Emotional State**: Heart beating, longing, trusting all day; only thought when will he come; only feeling to sleep and wake upon; suffered three days absence with distress; eyes filled with tears; kept packet of George's letters in chamber
- **Recent Developments**: That very evening (after George received money) wrote him tenderest of long letters; heart overflowing with tenderness but still foreboding evil; asked what caused Mr. Osborne's dark looks; wondered if difference had arisen between him and her papa; noted her poor papa returned so melancholy from City, all alarmed at home; four pages filled with loves, fears, hopes, forebodings

**Captain Dobbin** [CHARACTER]
- Friend of George Osborne; attentive and kind; enjoys military stories
- Calls to look for George at Osborne house; has been calling at Sedley house seeking George; when George wasn't there, only found Amelia; offered to fetch George but George never came
- Confronted George after Mrs. Major O'Dowd revealed engagement; George became furious, accused Dobbin of betraying secret; George vented frustration; upon reflection, apologized
- **Assistance to George**: Got George out of scrapes; when Crawley of Guards won money from George, Dobbin prevented ruin; accommodated Osborne with pound notes for Amelia's present; applauded visit decision; urged George comfort Amelia and write long letter; warned George shouldn't sermonise him
- **Status**: Blushed and looked awkward remembering Sedley house visits; would have given bank-note for one of Amelia's letters; takes George to be Admirable Crichton

**Old Mr. Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant in tallow trade and City of London; puffy, solemn, yellow-faced; black eyebrows; large white waistcoat; hirsute
- When returning from City troubled or displeased, shows it plainly in face; gave Amelia surly grunt when she saluted him, dropped her little hand without attempt to hold it
- Upon entering drawing-room and seeing Amelia, his face showed heart was disturbed; looked gloomily at eldest daughter, silently asking "Why the devil is she here?"
- At dinner, made curt remarks respecting soup and fish; cursed Billingsgate; lapsed into silence; swallowed sundry glasses of wine; looked more and more terrible until George's arrival
- **Pride in George's Position**: Praises George's consorting with nobility; boasts about great men he meets; falls down prostrate, basking in aristocratic acquaintances; introduced names into daily conversation
- **Attitude toward Sedley**: States Sedley made his fortune; has shown gratitude; does not like looks of Sedley's affairs; claims Mr. Chopper, chief clerk, agrees; states Hulker & Bullock looking shy at Sedley; suspects Sedley dabbling on own account; believes Jeune Amelie was Sedley's, taken by Yankee privateer Molasses; declares "unless I see Amelia's ten thousand down you don't marry her"; will "have no lame duck's daughter in my family"
- **Financial Support to George**: Instructed George to call on Mr. Chopper in City; George received document from Chopper and exchanged it at Hulker & Bullock's for pocketful of money (COMPLETED)
- **Current Status**: Relaxed somewhat after George's arrival and praise of wine; agreed to ring for claret; adopted rather cordial manner while discussing matters of importance

**Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; perfect celebrated "blood" or dandy about town; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; belonged to household troops around Prince Regent; fought three bloody duels; very large, six feet high; very generous with money
- Over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate; all young men at Wattier's and Cocoa-Tree swear by him
- Miss Crawley almost adopted him; disliked Mr. Pitt; always paid his dueling debts; designated for fifty thousand pounds in will per Rector
- **Recent Developments**: Rode up from Knightsbridge Barracks next day after Rebecca's arrival at Miss Crawley's house in Park Lane; found Miss Crawley ill in bed; found Miss Briggs (dame de compagnie) in tears, denied admission to sickroom by Rebecca; Rebecca came tripping down from sickroom, put little hand into his as he stepped forward eagerly; gave glance of great scorn at Briggs; beckoned Rawdon to back drawing-room, led him downstairs to dining-parlour; they talked ten minutes (discussed symptoms of invalid); parlour bell rung briskly; Rawdon came out curling mustachios; mounted black charger pawing in straw; looked in at dining-room window managing horse; young person (Rebecca) seen at window then vanished
- **Status**: Increasingly attached to Rebecca; under her influence; Miss Crawley still facilitates their proximity; Rawdon now visits her in London during her role as Miss Crawley's companion

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune from mother; silly and romantic; disliked Mr. Pitt; very attached to Rawdon; adores imprudent matches; approves Lord Nelson's character
- Insists Rebecca sit at dinners; mocks society with her; orders Rawdon lead her in to dinner, Rebecca follow with cushion
- **Recent Developments**: Returned from Hants to house in Park Lane in travelling chariot with lozenge on panels; discontented female in green veil on rumble; large confidential man on box; carriage windows shut; fat spaniel on discontented female's lap; taken from carriage by domestics and young lady (Rebecca) as bundle of shawls; conveyed upstairs to bed in warmed chamber; messengers sent for physician and medical man; they came, consulted, prescribed, vanished; now ill and under Rebecca's nursing care

**Sir Pitt Crawley, Baronet** [CHARACTER]
- Old, stumpy, short, vulgar, very dirty man; shining bald head, leering red face, twinkling grey eyes; perpetually grinning; country accent; swears greatly; could not spell
- Takes pipe and beer talking to John Horrocks about livestock; espied Rawdon and Rebecca from study-window; swore great oaths

**Mr. Pitt Crawley (Eldest Son)** [CHARACTER]
- Pale, thin, ugly, silent; studied ancient and modern orators; Private Secretary to Lord Binkie; Attache to Pumpernickel Legation ten years; exceedingly proud of French skills; turned country gentleman; wrote pamphlet on Malt; friend of Wilberforce; gave speech at Quashimaboo-Aid Society; criticizes Rebecca's backgammon as godless

**Mrs. Bute Crawley (Rector's Wife)** [CHARACTER]
- Amiable former Miss Pinkerton pupil; little, black-faced old woman in turban
- Initially reported Rebecca as artful hussy; now taken great fancy to her; invited girls to Rectory; complimented Rebecca and Rawdon's country-dance steps; **PLAN (active)** hopes to secure Rebecca as piano professor for her children

**Reverend Bute Crawley (Rector)** [CHARACTER]
- Tall, stately, jolly; far more popular in county than Sir Pitt; pulled stroke-oar at college; attends every fight, race, regatta, ball, election within twenty miles; best fisherman in county
- Deeply resentful of Rawdon's position in Miss Crawley's will; claims Rawdon has robbed him; speculates Miss Crawley drops in year; expects only thirty thousand to divide among family

**Miss Briggs (Dame de Compagnie)** [CHARACTER]
- Hastened to Miss Crawley's house upon hearing of illness; wished to nurse her; denied admission to Miss Crawley's apartment by Rebecca
- **Emotional State**: Found in tears alone in drawing-room by Rawdon; crushed affections; poor old red nose; felt desertion keenly by Rebecca; bitterly moaned fickleness of Matilda (Miss Crawley); placable and soft-hearted; pushed out hand in response to Rebecca's appeal for friendship; forced to accept Rebecca's assurance she would leave after two weeks; felt displacement despite reassurance; observed Rebecca's displacement of all other attendants

**Mrs. Firkin (Lady's Maid)** [CHARACTER]
- Pushed into Miss Crawley's apartment while Rebecca was attending her; bustled about during Rebecca's absence for dinner
- **Status**: Was attending Miss Crawley; eliminated from nursing role by Rebecca ("Thank you, Mrs. Firkin, that will quite do..."); came downstairs in tempest of jealousy forced to confine in her own bosom; passed landing carrying spoon and gruel-basin as neglected female

**Other Characters**: Mr. Chopper (chief clerk to Old Mr. Osborne); Mr. Driver (clerk at desk); Mr. Quill (cashier at Hulker & Bullock's); Young Bullock (banker); Mr. Bowls (Miss Crawley's large confidential butler, eavesdropped at keyhole during Rawdon-Rebecca interview); discontented female (Miss Crawley's maid); other minor figures

## Critical Facts and Status
- Rebecca now in London in position of companion/nurse to Miss Crawley; successfully displaced Miss Briggs and Mrs. Firkin; controls access to sickroom; maintains calculated politeness while asserting authority
- Old John Sedley observed leaving banker's parlour looking dismal (timing coincides with George receiving money)
- Young Bullock did not come grinning out of parlour as had been his wont in former years; banker behavior changed
- Hulker & Bullock's staff (Mr. Quill, Mr. Driver) exchanged knowing winks regarding Mr. Sedley's situation
- Amelia unaware of George's actual financial transaction; worries instead about Mr. Osborne's dark looks and her father's melancholy
- Amelia's letters continue to express innocent love and concern
- Rawdon visits Rebecca in her new role; remains under her influence
- Cotho Brackwood moved from Mirecombe to Dunholt (CHANGED from prior summary)
- Feena Stenworth followed Cotho to Dunholt within month (ADDED fact)
